title: fix(app-shell): a failed option roster is not a roster that answered “absent”
body:
Fixes #9651

objectui#8862 gave `InspectorSelectField` a `loading` term, so a valid stored value is no longer flagged `(not in object)` while its roster is in flight. A fetch that **fails** leaves the same residue as a successful fetch that found nothing -- an empty `options` array with nothing in flight -- so the flag still fired, and unlike the pending window it never cleared. A correctly bound key wore the marker **permanently**, and nothing on screen said the request had failed.

## The file, and the lines that decide the flag

The card named a symbol and no path. `InspectorSelectField` is defined in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/_shared.tsx`; the decision was the `label:` ternary inside the synthesised row, which chose between the raw value and `unknownValueLabel(current)` on the `loading` boolean, next to an `isUnknownValue` membership test over `options`.

## Reproduction first -- three states, one instrument, measured in the real renderer

Driven through the real `ViewColumnInspector` with a real `useObjectFields` over a metadata client the test settles, on the unrepaired tree:

| arm | trigger text | elements with `role="status"` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| roster IN FLIGHT (control -- objectui#8862's delivery) | `amount` | none |
| roster ANSWERED, value genuinely absent (control -- the flag must still fire) | `amount (not in object)` | none |
| roster ANSWERED, value present (reference) | `Total \| amount` | none |
| roster **FAILED** (the subject) | `amount (not in object)` | **none** |

The failure arm was byte-identical to the genuinely-absent arm, and said nothing at all about the failure. After the repair the same instrument reads `amount` for the failure arm, with one notice carrying `Options could not be loaded 503 Service Unavailable`; the three control arms are unchanged.

## The shape, and why there is no fourth arm behind it

A second boolean beside `loading` was the obvious repair and is the wrong one: three facts in two booleans is how this arrived, and four facts in three booleans leaves five combinations nothing defines. The primitive now reads **one discriminated state** -- the `LoadState` union the metadata-admin loaders already share (objectui#5170 / objectui#5169, `views/metadata-admin/loadState.ts`) -- through an **exhaustive** switch whose `default` leg binds the narrowed value to `never`. So there are no combinations left to leave undefined, and a new arm added to that union stops compiling in `rosterVerdict` rather than falling silently into one of the existing answers. That is mechanical, not remembered.

`loading?: boolean` is **replaced** by `roster?: LoadState`, not joined by a sibling flag. Omitting the prop still means "synchronous roster, already answered", which is what the roughly forty call sites with a literal `options` array pass -- pinned as its own case.

`InspectorComboField` deliberately keeps its boolean `loading`: that prop only picks the trigger's placeholder text, it decides no claim about the author's data, so it has no fault arm to be blind to.

## What the field DOES on a failure -- followed from the tree, not invented

The tree already answered this for the SchemaForm widget family. The shared `PickerLoadFailure` block (`views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx`, objectui#5170) states that the list could not be loaded, shows the cause, makes **no** claim in either direction about whether options exist, and every picker keeps the control that lets the author see and edit the stored value, because a failed catalog must not also block authoring. `AddFieldPopover` renders the same fact as a warn-toned hint with the cause, checked before its empty branch.

The inspector row now does those same three things in the space it has: the stored value stays legible and unflagged, a notice with `role="status"` names the failure and its cause, and the picker stays editable. Suppressing the flag alone would have traded a wrong message for no message. Wording comes from the call site (this module has no locale in scope, the same contract `unknownValueLabel` already has), and the call sites pass the localized copy objectui#5170 already landed, `engine.form.optionsLoadFailedTitle` -- so no new i18n key.

Threaded at the four `InspectorSelectField` call sites that take an async roster, each from the `error` its own loader has published all along and every one of them dropped: `ViewColumnInspector`'s field-key picker (`useObjectFields`), `ReportDefaultInspector`'s dataset binding (`useDatasetCatalog`), and both of that inspector's chart axes (`useDatasetSemantics`). The pair-to-state adaptation is written once, as `rosterFrom`, so the precedence it encodes -- a reported fault outranks an in-flight retry -- cannot be re-derived differently per site.

## Pins -- all three states, plus the two arms that already worked

`_shared.rosterFailure.test.tsx` (primitive) and `ViewColumnInspector.rosterFailure.test.tsx` (end to end, through the real hook). Both drive the component; no source-text assertions. The in-flight and genuinely-absent arms are pinned as controls in both files, so a later repair cannot re-open them, and the objectui#8862 pins were migrated to the new spelling with their asserted frames unchanged.

## Reverse verification -- five ablations, each on the committed fix

Each mutation is applied by an anchor-checked replacement, proven to have landed by blob hash plus an on-disk count in both directions, run, then restored with `git checkout HEAD --` and proven restored by hash equality **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`, under a trap on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths.

| ablation | rows that went red | rows that stayed green |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `error` arm collapsed to `answered` (the pre-fix reading) | 3 -- the failure-suppression rows, both files | pending, answered, notice, unknown-value |
| the failure notice deleted | 4 -- only the notice rows | flag suppression, editability, all controls |
| `loaded` collapsed to `silent` (never flag) | 3 -- the true negatives, including objectui#8862's own | everything else |
| `loading` collapsed to `answered` | 9 -- every pending-arm row in both objectui#8862 suites | the failure and answered rows |
| omitted prop collapsed to `silent` | 8 -- the whole objectui#8488 unknown-value family | the stateful arms |

One correction the ablations forced: the first run of the notice ablation turned the end-to-end flag-suppression and editability rows red too, because they used the notice as their settle gate -- for want of a settle, not for their own reason. Those rows now flush the rejection explicitly, and the re-run shows the two halves of the repair failing independently. That is the second commit on this branch.

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` and `lint` -- `VERDICT command-exit 0`; eslint reports **0 errors**. One new `react-refresh/only-export-components` warning on `_shared.tsx` for the `rosterFrom` export, a class that file already carries five times.
- Gates, all exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:i18n-call-site-keys`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-claims`.
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on this PR's seven paths: **NOT GOVERNED**.

## Cross-tree sweep

The concept is "every test that reaches `InspectorSelectField`", not "every test that spells it". A reverse-import walk from the three changed modules over `packages/app-shell/src` reaches 198 modules, 152 of them test files, and 82 of the reached files sit outside `views/metadata-admin/` -- the package barrel is in the closure, so narrowing below the package is **not** provable. The whole `packages/app-shell/` tree was therefore run, which is the package's own `pnpm test` scope. No other package imports these modules.

## Pending-changeset sweep

`.changeset/8862-inspector-select-roster-pending.md`, front matter `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`, two paragraphs:

1. "The primitive gains the term it was missing, `loading`" -- that prop no longer exists under that name.
2. "Still open and deliberately not guessed here: a roster whose fetch FAILED also resolves to an empty array with `loading` back to false, so the marker still fires on a load error." -- that arm is closed by this change.

Not edited here: it is another card's declaration. Flagged for the seat.

`.changeset/8488-inspector-select-unknown-value.md` carries a "known boundary" paragraph about the pending arm; that was already historical after objectui#8862 and is not made false by this diff.
